about: Engines beside the screen (DESIGN 5.12, N5): an engine declared `beside the screen` runs where its canvas is drawn (`canvas ... runs Screen`), one instance per canvas, from when its window opens until it closes. It speaks the engine interface of conformance/engines.json and exports `clarity_tick` and `clarity_draw` besides it. At every frame the renderer calls `clarity_tick` with the milliseconds since the last frame (`[ms]`; the first frame gives 0), then `clarity_draw` (`[]`), whose value is the canvas's shapes in its units, as a draw handler's (conformance/drawing.json). With `on open` (`opens`), `clarity_open` runs once, when the instance is made, before the first frame. The renderer skips a frame while the engine is still busy with the last one, so frames never pile up. `engine` is screen.wasm, built from engines/screen: it draws a dot that moves 1 unit every 10 ms and the time it has run. `frames` gives the ticks in order and the shapes after each. A frame that fails, or runs longer than the engine's time limit, ends the engine: the canvas shows `fails` in place of its drawing, the renderer calls it no more, and the window works on. `fails` cases give the ticks before and the tick that fails.
